mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registrar or competent authority in the foreign investor's home jurisdiction (e.g., Delaware Secretary of State, Singapore ACRA, UK Companies House)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-member origin: obtain the official certificate and, if required by SAMR, a notarized copy; obtain an Apostille certificate from the home-state competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State or ACRA); arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member origin: authenticate the certificate through the home foreign ministry and then obtain consular legalization from the PRC Embassy or Consulate; arrange certified Chinese translation. The Apostille path and consular legalization path are parallel alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Incumbency for non-common-law jurisdictions)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of companies or corporate registry in the foreign investor's jurisdiction, or licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-member origin: if issued by a government registrar, apply directly for Apostille from the competent authority; if issued by a private agent, notarize the agent's signature first and then apply for Apostille; arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member origin: notarize, authenticate through the local foreign ministry, then legalize through the PRC Embassy or Consulate; arrange certified Chinese translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive; do not combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney approving incorporation of the WFOE and authorizing the local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor, with signatures notarized under the law of the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-member origin: notarize the signatures before a local notary public; obtain an Apostille certificate from the competent national or subnational authority; arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member origin: notarize the signatures, obtain authentication from the local foreign affairs or justice authority, then obtain consular legalization from the PRC Embassy or Consulate; arrange certified Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative authentication regimes and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association, Constitutional Documents, or equivalent constitutive extract of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official registrar's certified copy, or notarized copy issued by the foreign investor's registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-member origin: apply for a certified copy from the registrar, or notarize a company-issued copy; obtain Apostille from the competent authority; arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member origin: notarize the copies, authenticate through the relevant home authority, then legalize through the PRC consular post; arrange certified Chinese translation. The Apostille path and the consular path are separate, co-equal alternatives and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the foreign investor's relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Branch or relationship manager of the foreign investor's commercial bank, issued on bank letterhead with original signature and seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-member origin: notarize the bank officer's signature and authority; obtain Apostille from the relevant competent authority; arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member origin: notarize the bank officer's signature, obtain local Foreign Ministry authentication, and then obtain PRC consular legalization; arrange certified Chinese translation. Use only one of the two paths, never both in sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening shall be completed before onboarding and repeated at least quarterly and before every capital call, distribution, or change of beneficial ownership. Screen all natural-person UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, and senior compliance officers, and all legal-person members with more than 25% ownership, using fuzzy matching and alias detection against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications, EU and UK HMT sanctions, PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Commerce sanctions lists, Interpol Red Notices, AMAC blacklists, and China's domestic criminal justice watchlists. For any match, apply immediate asset freeze reporting to PBOC and SAMR within 24 hours. Enhanced due diligence must include source of wealth, source of funds, beneficial ownership chains through trusts and nominee structures, adverse media review, and high-risk jurisdiction nexus. All screening results, false-positive dispositions, and escalation decisions must be timestamped, signed, and preserved for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) 'National Enterprise Name Registration and Reservation System' and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (credit.gsxt.gov.cn), together with the local municipal SAMR online name-clearance and entity registration portal for the intended registered district
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Enterprise name law requires a four-tier structure: administrative division; trade name; industry or business feature; and legal form. The legal name must be written in simplified Chinese characters. A foreign investor's name may be rendered in pinyin or Chinese-character transliteration. Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and symbols are not permitted in the legal name unless specifically approved by competent authorities. The legal form for a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company must use the statutory Chinese morphograms for 'limited company' (youxian gongsi) and must not indicate partnership status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon online rejection, the applicant may revise and resubmit the name once, replacing any conflicting trade-name token or adding a distinctive element such as a geographic qualifier or investor's transliterated surname. The reserved name may be extended once for an additional 30 days before expiration through the SAMR portal if incorporation is pending due to cross-border notarization or consular legalization. For formal rejection on grounds of confusion, prohibited words, or bad faith, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the next-higher SAMR authority within 60 days of the adverse notice under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, or commence an administrative lawsuit within six months under the Administrative Litigation Law. Simultaneously, the applicant may submit a written petition and complaint through the SAMR petition office and the national 12315 market-regulation complaint platform, attaching the proposed name, foreign registration proof, and ministerial approvals for any sensitive token. The appeal must show calculated distinctiveness against existing trade names in the target administrative division and industry classification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial-mailbox-only address is not permissible for a WFOE operating as a venture capital general partner. The PRC Company Law, SAMR registration rules, and State Taxation Administration practice require a registered address that corresponds to a real, usable physical office. Local tax authorities will reject tax registration and banks will decline a corporate account where the address is only a virtual mailbox. AMAC private fund manager registration rules require physical business premises, a permanent place of management, local compliance staffing, and business continuity. Pilot Free-Trade-Zone cluster or shared registration may be available for ordinary service companies, but financial-investment and fund-management entities are generally excluded or subject to a substantive-presence condition. Therefore, a dedicated serviced office with a lease, signage, and staffing is the minimum acceptable commercial substance for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection checklist to be ready at all times: (1) current lease agreement with rent receipts; (2) office signage and directory listing; (3) employees or responsible staff present during normal business hours; (4) fixed telecommunications and internet in the entity's name; (5) corporate books, seals, and statutory records kept at the address; (6) board resolutions and annual meeting minutes executed at the place of management; (7) payroll, social insurance, and tax filing records tied to the address; and (8) the written compliance manual required for AMAC registration. Quantified unannounced inspection risk by municipal market-supervision and tax authorities: 30-40% within the first 12 months for a virtual or unmarked serviced-office address; 15-20% for a serviced office with signage but minimal staff; and 5-10% for a fully staffed physical office with complete records. The 'double random, one open' inspection program and tax field surveys before general-taxpayer designation materially increase the probability of an on-site visit for a medium-risk enhanced VC-GP entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23, 26-32, 37-41, 46-48, 53, 56-59 and 68-70; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 16, 18, 21 and 28; Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (2022), Articles 2, 8-12 and 17; and the latest Foreign Investment Negative List issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and the Ministry of Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); local provincial/municipal Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), including the foreign-invested enterprise registration windows of the AMR and, where applicable, the relevant Pilot Free Trade Zone sub-bureau.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form, together with the application for a Unified Social Credit Code Business License and the approved Company Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum paid-up registered capital is imposed on an ordinary WFOE limited liability company under the 2023 Company Law. However, Article 47 requires shareholders to pay subscribed capital in full within five years from the date of establishment unless a shorter period is stated in the articles. Capital can be contributed in cash, equipment, intellectual property or equity if lawfully valued. No blocked escrow account is mandated by SAMR for formation. For private fund manager registration, the Asset Management Association of China (AMAC) generally expects paid-up registered capital of at least RMB 2 million, together with a demonstrably adequate office and compliance infrastructure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME IN ENGLISH] (COMPANY) / [REGISTERED CHINESE NAME] (WFOE), a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company organized under the laws of the People's Republic of China.

WHEREAS, the Company has been incorporated by the sole shareholder pursuant to the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision) and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019); and WHEREAS, the Board of Directors of the Company has the power to adopt initial governance resolutions per the Company's Articles of Association.

NOW, THEREFORE, upon motion duly made, seconded, and unanimously adopted, the Board of Directors, exercising all authority conferred by law and the Articles, hereby RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

1. Registered Capital and Share Subscription. The Board acknowledges that the Company has an initial registered capital of RMB [___] divided into [___] units. The share subscription and capital contribution schedule attached as exhibit are ratified. The Board directs management to open a separate capital contribution account and to deposit or call contributions only in accordance with the Articles and Article 47 of the Company Law, requiring full payment of subscribed capital within five years after establishment.

2. Banking and Signatory Authorization. The Board designates [Bank Name] as the Company's principal banker. The legal representative and the finance director, or any two of the legal representative, the finance director and the chairman, are authorized jointly to open bank accounts, execute account mandates, issue capital call notices, receive subscription funds, and make SWIFT transfers. For each transaction above RMB [___], the directors shall present a written treasury instruction.

3. Registered Office. The registered office at [Address] is adopted as the Company's statutory seat. Management is directed to file the lease and to maintain the office as the site of the Company's statutory registers and books.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The following officers are elected and appointed effective as of the date of the Business License: [Name] as Legal Representative and Chairman; [Name] as Director and General Manager; [Name] as Company Supervisor. The officers are directed to preserve records, file all tax returns, and execute incorporation-related contracts.

5. Delegation of Operating Mandate. The Board authorizes the General Manager to complete AMAC private fund manager registration, execute fund formation agreements, open a foreign exchange capital account, and take all steps needed to launch early-stage technology funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation, negative-list screening and business-scope assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the local 'One-Stop' investment service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant must first screen the proposed business scope against the current Foreign Investment Access Negative List to confirm that venture capital fund management and general partner services are permitted. Using the local AMR's online service, submit a name reservation application for the Chinese legal name and an optional English company name. The name should reflect 'venture capital' or 'equity investment fund management' and must not include words requiring separate financial licensing, such as 'securities' or 'bank', unless such license is already held. The AMR will conduct a national name conflict check, issue a name reservation notice, and advise whether a preliminary financial regulator consultation is required.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Certificate of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
Passport or national identity document of the proposed legal representative
Power of attorney if an agent is used
Description of the proposed business scope and simplified ISIC code 6499
Letter undertaking lawful private fund management operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is queried on grounds of identical or confusingly similar corporate names, file a revised name or submit a written distinction letter from the prior holder within ten working days. If the business scope wording is challenged as sensitive, narrow the scope and remove references to licensed bank, securities or insurance activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, apostille and translation of foreign corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public office in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction and, where required, Chinese embassy or consulate; for Hague Convention jurisdictions, the competent apostille authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign shareholder's certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and board resolution authorizing the China WFOE must be notarized and legalized. For most jurisdictions, the Hague Apostille Convention applies to documents issued after China's accession; an apostille is sufficient. For non-apostille jurisdictions, consular legalization at the Chinese embassy or consulate is required. All foreign-language instruments must be translated into Chinese by a registered translation enterprise, and each translation must be certified as truthfully corresponding to the original. The legal representative and director appointments should be evidenced by the original notarized passports and by an authorized signatory list.
required_dossiers: Notarized and apostilled or legalized certificate of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
Certificate of good standing or equivalent official statement
Foreign shareholder's board resolution authorizing the establishment of the WFOE
Notarized passport and identity documents of the proposed directors and legal representative
Certified Chinese translations of all foreign documents with translator's seal
Parent company audited financial statements if requested by AMR or the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AMR challenges the legality or sufficiency of the apostille or legalization, obtain a supplementary apostille from the issuing authority or re-notarize the instruments in China. If a translation is rejected, replace it with a translation by a registered translation company and attach a translator's certification declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of WFOE establishment registration and issuance of business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), foreign-invested enterprise registration window, or the SAMR-approved online registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant must complete the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form, verify the name reservation notice, and submit the original notarized shareholder documents together with the approved Chinese translation. The Articles of Association must contain the company name, address, purpose, registered capital, contribution schedule, board composition, supervisor, legal representative, meeting rules and liquidation provisions as required by SAMR's model articles. If the legal representative is not physically present, submit a notarized power of attorney. The local AMR will examine the business scope for negative-list compliance and, if all requirements are satisfied, will issue the Unified Social Credit Code Business License.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form
Company Articles of Association in Chinese
Name reservation notice
Notarized and legalized foreign shareholder documents with certified Chinese translations
Certificate of registered office, comprising a valid lease agreement and property ownership certificate or rental certification
Appointment certificates for legal representative, directors and supervisor
Capital contribution schedule and bank capital contribution account commitment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AMR issues a rectification notice, cure the non-material irregularities within fifteen working days and resubmit electronically. If the application is rejected for insufficient legalization, provide apostilled documents and corrected translations. If AMR requests the ultimate beneficial owner declaration, submit an accurate UBO statement and supporting chain-of-ownership documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation corporate organization, bank account activation and tax/social registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraving company; licensed commercial bank; State Taxation Administration (STA) local municipal office; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) or delegated bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten working days of receiving the business license, apply to a public-security-licensed engraving company to create the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and contract seal. Open a basic RMB deposit account and a separate foreign currency capital account at a licensed commercial bank; provide the original business license, unified social credit code and board banking resolutions. Complete tax registration with the local STA office, pay any stamp duty on registered capital and accounting books, register with social insurance and housing fund bureaus, and file foreign investment information with the Ministry of Commerce or an authorized bank. For capital contributions from abroad, complete SAFE registration and preserve bank receipts for capital verification.
required_dossiers: Business License original and duplicate
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Seal engraving authorization document
Legal representative identity document
Bank account application forms and Articles of Association
Company resolution authorizing bank signatories and banking authority
SAFE foreign exchange registration form if foreign currency capital is to be remitted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening for enhanced AML/KYC reasons, provide complete beneficial ownership declarations and a fresh board resolution designating the legal representative and finance director. If SAFE registration is delayed, use the delegated bank approval procedure and request a provisional processing receipt from the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Private fund manager registration with AMAC and fund deployment readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Asset Management Association of China (AMAC) Private Fund Filing Center, under the regulatory supervision of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after incorporation, the WFOE, if acting as a private fund general partner, must apply to AMAC for private fund manager registration. The online application must include the business license, articles of association, capital verification report, legal representative and senior management questionnaires, compliance and anti-money laundering manuals, information technology and business continuity policies, and a credible description of the first private equity or venture capital fund. AMAC will verify paid-up capital generally of at least RMB 2 million, office facilities, legal qualifications and key personnel. Successful registration is a mandatory license before capital can be raised; the entity must launch its first fund within twelve months of registration or the manager registration may lapse.
required_dossiers: AMAC online registration application form
Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Capital verification report or bank statements proving paid-up registered capital
Legal representative and senior management resumes and identity documents
Compliance, risk management, anti-money laundering and conflict-of-interest manuals
Registered office lease agreement and business operations plan
First fund formation roadmap and targeted capital source description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AMAC issues an advisory opinion or requires rectification, respond in writing within thirty working days and provide supplemental audit or source-of-funds evidence. If registration is rejected, remedy the stated grounds and submit a new application. If the twelve-month fund filing deadline is at risk, file an explanation and expedite the first private fund filing before the deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for industrial and physical licensing because the entity is a pure financial services and venture capital general partner conducting office-based asset management. The relevant financial licensing authority is the Asset Management Association of China (AMAC), subject to the supervision of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Fund Manager Registration with AMAC, together with the Business License authorizing 'venture capital investment management' or 'equity investment fund management' activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) - Not Applicable because no physical construction, manufacturing installation or industrial facility is involved; an ordinary leased office is exempt from environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Environmental Registration not required. The registered office is a service office with no production equipment, chemical storage or hazardous waste generation, and therefore does not fall within the EIA Classification List (2021 Edition) project categories.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None apply to process wastewater, VOCs or hazardous waste for this office-only venture capital manager. The entity must only comply with municipal solid waste sorting and general office building safety standards. If a dedicated server room is installed, local data center energy-efficiency and e-waste disposal rules will apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required for the office premises: the local Fire and Rescue Department must issue a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate or Fire Safety Acceptance Record before the office is occupied under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China. No civil defense permit, dangerous goods storage approval or structural load inspection is triggered for an office-only financial company. The WFOE must maintain evacuation signage, fire extinguishers and records of fire drills. Workplace safety approval for industrial workshops is Not Applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; the official online fiscal portal is the National Unified Electronic Taxpayer Portal (e-Tax), operated by STA and provincial-level tax authorities for registration, filing, assessment, invoice administration and export tax refund processes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Mainland China WFOE is formed through the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Upon issuance of the business license, the WFOE receives a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). The USCC is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for all Chinese taxes, including enterprise income tax, VAT, stamp duty and withholding taxes. Tax data is automatically transmitted from SAMR to STA, making a separate tax registration certificate unnecessary. Within 30 calendar days after the business license date, the WFOE must complete the tax information registration report through the e-Tax portal, confirming the entity name, USCC, registered address, business scope, legal representative, shareholders, industry classification (ISIC 6499/NAICS 525910), accounting standards, bank account details, authorized agents, and forecast of taxable turnover. The WFOE must also register as a VAT taxpayer: as a general taxpayer if forecast annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, or as a small-scale taxpayer below that threshold, with an elective general-taxpayer application if proper accounting and premises are established. In addition, because the WFOE is a venture-capital general partner making fee, carry and dividend payments to non-resident funds, it must complete withholding-agent registration for Chinese-source payments to non-residents; the non-resident fund may separately be required to obtain a Chinese non-resident enterprise TIN through the withholding or direct filing route. Finally, the WFOE must apply through e-Tax for invoice types and quota, and obtain the digital tax-control certificate needed to issue VAT invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the WFOE is a resident Chinese limited liability company taxed under the Enterprise Income Tax Law on worldwide income, with no pass-through treatment. It is also a VAT taxable person; its VAT status is either general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer depending on turnover.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification; China has no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election that changes a WFOE's status to pass-through. The only material election is VAT: a small-scale taxpayer may voluntarily elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer if it can demonstrate fixed business premises, sound books, and reliable accounting, and may not revert without approval. Enterprise income tax group consolidation is not available for separate WFOEs; no partnership-style pass-through is permitted for a WFOE itself.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) administered under the PRC VAT Law and the State Taxation Administration implementing rules; the standard statutory VAT rate is 13% for goods, with reduced rates of 9% for certain goods and services and 6% for financial and modern services, the latter being applicable to the venture-capital GP's management and advisory fees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 generally requires mandatory registration as a general VAT taxpayer. Small-scale taxpayer status applies to annual taxable sales at or below RMB 5,000,000, and small-scale taxpayers enjoy a monthly VAT exemption of RMB 100,000 subject to STA policy updates. Voluntary general taxpayer registration is available below the threshold in limited cases. For a venture-capital GP, management fees and fund-advisory fees are taxable at 6%, while carried interest is generally not VAT-taxable if it is an investment-return allocation rather than remuneration for services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory digital invoice system under the STA's national electronic invoice platform. General VAT taxpayers must issue VAT invoices, including special VAT invoices, through the tax-control digital invoicing system; all invoice data is transmitted in real time to the STA central tax database, with automatic validation of taxpayer IDs, invoice numbers, tax codes, rates and amounts. The system applies anti-fraud digital stamping using the taxpayer's tax-control digital seal, and dynamic invoice quota management is used to prevent fictitious issuance. After the Golden Tax System Phase IV rollout, invoice data is reconciled with SAMR registration, corporate bank account settlement and customs clearance data. Large taxpayers or enterprises issuing a high volume of invoices are required or encouraged to connect their ERP systems to the electronic invoice platform through certified APIs to obtain invoice numbers and perform real-time invoice clearance. Digital invoices are the default; paper special VAT invoices are restricted to transitional cases and must be reported through the same tax-control system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: 0% VAT, i.e. exemption with refund, is available only where the goods are actually exported through a customs supervision place; the exporter is a VAT taxpayer; the export is evidenced by a valid customs export declaration with the correct HS code and declared value; and the export sales proceeds are repatriated to China in accordance with SAFE rules, normally within 180 days, with supporting bank foreign-exchange receipts. For cross-border services: zero-rating is limited to enumerated cross-border services under STA regulations; a venture-capital GP's separately charged fund-administration or management services supplied to an overseas fund may qualify for cross-border VAT exemption rather than true zero-rating if the service is rendered entirely outside Mainland China, the recipient is an overseas entity, the benefit of the service is enjoyed outside China, and the taxpayer has filed the cross-border taxable service exemption record with the competent tax authority. Carried interest that represents an allocation of investment returns is not consideration for a taxable service and is outside the VAT base.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration Form (Customs Bill of Entry) with customs electronic release, export customs code, HS classification, quantity, FOB value and shipping marks; must be consistent with the export sales contract and invoice.
Bill of Lading, or Air Waybill, international rail or road consignment note, evidencing despatch and physical exit from China through the named customs port.

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), or bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher issued by the settlement bank, or SAFE system export-collection record, showing receipt of the export sales proceeds from the overseas buyer.
Export sales contract and commercial invoice detailing the overseas buyer, delivery terms, currency, unit price, total value, and payment milestones.
Packing list, customs inspection or weight list and, where applicable, the STA export tax-refund application data package electronically matching the customs clearance data and VAT invoice details.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are examined jointly by STA and Customs using cross-referenced electronic data, bank settlement data and invoice data. If the goods are not proven to have left China, or export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day deadline, or the documents are inconsistent, the zero-rating is reversed and output VAT becomes payable at the applicable statutory rate, 13% for goods or 6% for services, from the date of export, plus late-payment surcharge at 0.05% per day. A false export declaration, forged customs declaration, Bill of Lading, FIRC or fictitious invoice for the purpose of obtaining an export VAT refund is treated as fraudulent export tax-refund activity. Under Article 66 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection, the tax authority will recover the refunded VAT and impose a penalty of 1 to 5 times the amount fraudulently obtained. Under Article 63, evasion of VAT through false zero-rating is punishable by a penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax. Criminal liability, including imprisonment or criminal fines, may follow under the Criminal Law where the fraud amount exceeds the criminal threshold; the enterprise may also be placed on the tax-related serious untrustworthy entity list, with restrictions on directors, legal representatives, invoicing, financing and cross-border clearance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), delegated through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with current-account convertibility largely available for trade and service transactions, while the capital account remains closely regulated by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise formed as a venture capital general partner, the core distinction is that RMB converted from registered capital or operating receipts may be used for lawful current-item payments such as salaries, rent, management fees, professional fees and approved operational expenses without separate SAFE approval. However, capital-item movements, including investor equity injections, profit remittances, cross-border guarantees, intercompany loans, secondary equity transfers and outbound investments, require verifiable real transactions, purpose codes, supporting contracts and compliance under the Foreign Investment Negative List. Profit remittance is allowed only after audited statutory accounts, full tax settlement and administrative verification of distributable retained earnings; the bank requires a board resolution, tax payment certificates, audited financial statements and a detailed purpose statement. The venture capital GP will face enhanced scrutiny because capital calls, management fees and investment proceeds can be commingled if treasury controls are not transaction-mapped. Therefore, every cross-border flow must be referenced to a legal agreement, an arm's-length pricing rationale and a precise SAFE purpose classification, and the bank must be treated as a first-line compliance validator rather than a passive clearing gateway.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current PRC regulations, there is no mandatory percentage of export foreign-exchange receipts that must be sold to banks; exporters may retain 100 percent of repatriated export proceeds in a domestic foreign-exchange settlement account or voluntarily settle them into RMB at a designated bank. Nevertheless, all export performance and collection proceeds must be repatriated into the PRC banking system, verified through SAFE's electronic export monitoring framework, and reconciled with customs declarations. The standard statutory verification period for export receipts is generally 180 days from the customs export declaration date; where collection exceeds that window, the exporter must make a deferred collection registration or apply for an extension through the bank and SAFE's digital administration before the deadline lapses. For the WFOE GP, any incidental export or service-trade receipts must also be tagged with valid transaction background; capital account receipts from investors and fund-related events are treated under a different purpose-code matrix and are not subject to export surrender protocol.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI Capital Project Account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account and Ancillary Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Capital Call Operating Account and Payment Collection Account for Fund Administrative Activities
Foreign Exchange Settlement and Payment Account with Separate Capital Sub-Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally non-viable as a primary servicing bank. Offshore digital fintech EMIs are not licensed by the PBOC or SAFE to operate RMB clearing, act as designated foreign-exchange banks, access CIPS or hold a WFOE's capital account. Such EMIs are barred from performing FDI registration, capital verification, tax proofing and regulatory reporting that a licensed PRC bank must complete. An overseas EMI may only serve as an auxiliary receivable-collection vehicle outside China for ancillary purposes, and only if its due diligence standards are compatible; it can never replace a tier-1 domestic commercial bank for the regulated treasury and liquidity rail of a Chinese venture capital GP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical branch interview is generally required for the legal representative and senior designated compliance person at the bank holding the RMB basic deposit account. For a foreign legal representative, the branch will verify the original passport, valid visa or residence permit, company constitutional documents and notarized board or shareholder resolutions. Where the principal cannot attend in person, some tier-1 banks allow an authorized officer or nominated proxy to complete the account opening, provided the power of attorney is notarized at the PRC consulate or embassy, translated into certified Chinese and physically presented with original company seals. Fully remote video KYC is not a substitute for face-to-face verification, and the bank must complete the PBOC account anti-money laundering check and positive verification of the legal representative in the People's Bank of China legal-person account management system before the account can be activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layer offshore ownership involving Cayman or BVI holding vehicles obscures direct and indirect beneficial ownership of the WFOE GP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a signed full-chain beneficial ownership map from the WFOE to every ultimate natural person; notarized certificates of incumbency and certificate of good standing from each offshore registered agent; constitutional documents and share register for each intermediate entity; trust deeds and protector letters where applicable; passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners; source-of-wealth statements; and a formal corporate board resolution approving the establishment of the WFOE as general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital calls drawn from numerous offshore limited partners create unexpected payor names, high transaction velocity and potential commingling of investor funds with operating capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the fund limited partnership agreement, all executed subscription documents and side letters, investor capital commitment schedules, official capital call notices, investor AML/KYC certificates from the fund administrator, audited fund financial statements, independent bank statements showing the funding chain, and a compliance undertaking that every inbound wire must identify the paying investor, reference a unique capital call number and be traceable to the matching commitment ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Management fees, carried interest or expense reimbursements paid to affiliated offshore entities may be recharacterized as disguised profit remittances or abusive transfer pricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the investment management or advisory agreement, fee schedule and calculation model, itemized time and expense allocations, true invoices for each fee payment, meaningful evidence of services rendered, an audit trail showing portfolio monitoring deliverables, transfer pricing documentation aligned with Chinese rules and OECD principles, and a Chinese tax withholding certificate issued by the tax bureau if a cross-border service payment is made.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of FX-settled registered capital for domestic securities, entrusted loans, real estate or non-business investments could breach PRC Negative List and capital account payment restrictions for a venture capital GP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a SAFE compliance undertaking, an annual operating and investment budget, the fund mandate and investment policy documents, executed term sheets and investment agreements, proof that the proposed target is not on the prohibited Negative List, capital payment instruction forms with the correct purpose code, and an external PRC legal opinion confirming that the deployment falls within the WFOE's business scope and is not a prohibited capital-account movement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders must transfer the subscribed registered capital via SWIFT MT103 from their overseas bank account to the WFOE's foreign exchange capital account held at a licensed tier-1 PRC bank. Before the transfer, the WFOE must complete electronic FDI foreign exchange registration through the local SAFE framework and obtain the unique FDI security/verification code from the bank. The wire instruction must include the full name of the investor, the full name of the WFOE, the capital contribution reference and a foreign exchange purpose code corresponding to foreign direct investment equity injection. Upon receipt, the receiving bank will verify name, amount, currency, tax registration and paid-in capital schedule; if conversion into RMB is requested, the bank will credit the RMB capital settlement account and require the WFOE to submit a capital utilization plan. A Chinese certified public accountant should issue a capital verification report after each paid-in injection, and subsequent use of the capital, including investment into portfolio companies or payment of operating expenses, must be supported by signed agreements and purpose-specific documentation to satisfy the SAFE real-transaction and Negative List requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service-trade disbursements, including management fees, investment advisory fees, professional fees or licensing payments, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 through its licensed bank, attaching the underlying service contract, genuine invoice, evidence of completion, tax withholding certificate and the correct SAFE service-trade purpose code. For physical trade settlement, which is less typical for a venture capital GP, commercial letters of credit issued through the bank via SWIFT MT700/MT710 or documentary collections may be used when the WFOE or a portfolio company is importing equipment or purchasing goods. For the core venture capital treasury activities, outbound flows will normally be domestic RMB bank transfers to local target companies after FX settlement for equity investments, or MT103 wires to offshore service providers and intermediate fund structures; all such payments must be matched to a signed transaction, maintained in the bank's capital account payment log and submitted for SAFE cross-border transaction reporting where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts underwritten by a licensed onshore bank, subject to SAFE real-demand verification and supported by underlying current or capital account exposure
Plain vanilla CNY FX options purchased from a licensed bank, with premium-only settlement and no speculative writing of options by the WFOE
Onshore CNY/USD FX swaps for cash flow timing adjustments, provided the purpose is genuine and documented
Cross-currency swaps for long-term USD-denominated capital commitments and RMB operating needs, after obtaining bank risk approval and SAFE registration if required

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as onshore hedging instruments for the WFOE; they may be used only by an offshore affiliate with no CNY delivery obligation and with a separate legal opinion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (annual return and information publicity filing) filed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - local municipal/district SAMR market supervision bureau; data shared with other regulatory authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June each year for the preceding calendar year (annual filing window; no extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by 30 June results in inclusion on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Business Operations; the entity may be removed by filing the report within three years; if no corrective filing is made within three years, it is entered on the List of Enterprises Subject to Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Conduct, leading to administrative restrictions, credit sanctions and potential revocation/strike-off of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (PRC Foreign Investment Law integrated annual report for foreign-invested enterprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the one-stop annual report system, with automatic transmission to the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and the foreign investment information platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June each year for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing triggers inclusion in the abnormal operations list and an order to rectify; refusal to rectify may be punished with administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Law scale (up to RMB hundreds of thousands depending on severity) plus suspension of preferential foreign-investment treatment and credit downgrade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Enterprise Income Tax Annual Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) - local competent tax bureau through the electronic tax filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 31 May following the calendar year-end for the previous tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Overdue tax accrues a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day; late filing may incur administrative fines (typically RMB 2,000-10,000); under-declaration or non-declaration can produce penalties of 50%-100% of underpaid tax for intentional evasion, increased collection measures, credit rating downgrade, asset restraints and tax authority enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual PRC Statutory Audit of Financial Statements and approval of audited financial reports by shareholders/board
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent licensed PRC certified public accountant (CPA) firm; audited financial statements filed with SAMR in the annual report and retained for review by the STA, SAMR, MOFCOM and AMAC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements are to be prepared within four months after fiscal year-end; the independent audit must be completed before the 30 June annual report filing deadline and before the 31 May CIT final settlement deadline where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unaudited financial reports render annual report information defective and create abnormal-list exposure; false or dishonest audit reporting exposes directors and legal representatives to liabilities and penalties under the Company Law and Accounting Law, and fund managers may face AMAC registration suspension or cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AMAC annual report and compliance submission for the licensed private fund manager / venture capital general partner entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Asset Management Association of China (AMAC), operating under delegation from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of fiscal year end (for calendar-year managers: by 30 April of the following year); annual information updates in accordance with AMAC private fund manager rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or delayed submission places the manager on AMAC's abnormal operations list, suspends new fund filing privileges and may lead to cancellation of private fund manager registration, requiring wind-down of managed funds and exposing the entity to CSRC enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law, every limited liability company, including a WFOE, must prepare annual financial reports and have them audited by an accounting firm; there is no quantitative balance sheet, turnover or headcount exemption. The mandatory independent audit trigger arises from corporate form and, for this entity, from the AMAC private fund manager license requiring an annual audited financial report. Additionally, if the venture capital GP entity is treated as a financial or fund-management institution, sector regulators may impose audit requirements on fund-level assets regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (Chinese GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS; small non-public enterprises may apply the PRC Standards for Small Enterprises where eligible; tax accounts are reconciled to the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law and tax reporting rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: PRC law does not currently maintain a standalone public UBO register or a dedicated annual UBO confirmation filing. The WFOE must keep an internal record of shareholders, ultimate actual controllers and beneficial ownership, and must disclose ultimate foreign investors and actual controllers annually in the SAMR/MOFCOM annual foreign investment information report. Any shareholding transfer or change in shareholder/beneficial ownership must be reflected in the company's shareholders' register and filed with the local SAMR business registration authority within 30 days of the transfer; AMAC-registered fund managers must separately notify AMAC of changes to shareholders, actual controllers and senior managers within the timeline prescribed by AMAC rules (generally 10 working days).
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (director appointment, resignation and attendance records)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (equity pledge, security interest, guarantee and mortgage records)
Minute Book (shareholders' and directors' meeting minutes and resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 - US$3,500 per year for a registered address/legal representative/secretarial agent in major municipalities; premium commercial registered office lease is excluded
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 - US$8,000 for a simple WFOE; US$10,000 - US$30,000 for a venture capital GP entity with fund-level accounting, special purpose vehicles and AMAC compliance

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified High and New Technology Enterprises may use 15%; R&D expenses are generally super-deductible at 100% of actual qualifying outlay; accelerated depreciation is available for qualified fixed assets; certain Free Trade Zone and encouraged-industry policies can provide preferential 15% rates; for a Venture Capital General Partner (VC GP), carried interest is not separately privileged as capital gains under PRC Enterprise Income Tax, and a 5-year loss carry-forward applies in standard cases, with 10-year carry-forward for qualified High-Tech or Small and Medium-sized Technology Enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A) - Main Form A100000 plus ancillary schedules A101010, A105000, A106000, A107012 and A108000; filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration eTax portal or provincial electronic tax bureau
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional prepayment returns plus one annual final settlement return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment returns must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual final return and payment must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, which for a calendar-year WFOE is 31 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross income from management fees, carried interest, capital calls and investment-related service fees in CNY. If fees are invoiced to a non-resident affiliated fund or GP-affiliate, include the full gross amount, disclose the related-party transaction, and ensure any transfer pricing adjustment is made before filing. Do not treat carried interest as tax-exempt unless it is payment from an actual equity disposition with proper capital gain treatment. Cross-border management fees must be arm's length and supported by contemporaneous documentation.

Deduct only costs actually borne by the WFOE and substantiated by invoices/contracts. Service fees paid to a non-resident parent or offshore service provider are deductible only where the service is genuinely received, not duplicated, and supported by service agreements. The WFOE must withhold PRC Enterprise Income Tax at 10% where such fees are subject to Article 3(3), and VAT/withholding obligations must be completed before remittance or the deduction may be disallowed.

Gross receipts less cost of sales and directly attributable deductions. For a VC GP, management fee income from an offshore fund is Chinese-source operating income if the WFOE performs the service in China. Any unrealized carried interest is not reportable until earned and determinable; on liquidation of fund interests, gains must be characterised as ordinary business profit unless the ownership stake is an actual equity investment held by the WFOE.

Include selling, administrative, and financial expenses. Non-deductible expenses must be added back, including excessive related-party interest beyond the general debt-to-equity ratio (2:1 for non-financial enterprises), unapproved reserves, fines, and amounts paid to related parties lacking economic substance. Cross-border payments of interest and royalties must be benchmarked against arm's length rates and properly withheld, or the expenses may be recharacterized and disallowed.

After adjusting for permanent differences, loss carry-forwards, charitable deductions, and incentives, arrive at taxable income. The WFOE itself is the PRC taxpayer; income allocated to a non-resident fund investor is not taxable to that investor at entity level unless a profit distribution, dividend, or other withholding event occurs. Declare foreign tax credits on foreign-source income and do not claim treaty passthrough of losses from offshore fund vehicles.

Taxable income multiplied by the applicable rate (typically 25%, or 15% if a qualified high-tech enterprise). Apply available foreign tax credit, provisional prepaid CIT, and any required special tax adjustment interest. Separately, before any dividend remittance to a non-resident shareholder, the WFOE must file a withholding return and pay dividend withholding tax at the statutory or treaty reduced rate; the withholding liability is not boxed inside the annual CIT return but must be reconciled and disclosed in the related-party and withholding schedules. Failure to report can trigger penalties and loss of treaty protection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalised under the Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) Article 62: the tax authority may order filing and impose fines up to RMB 2,000, increased to RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious or repeated failure. Late payment attracts a surcharge of 0.05% per day on the unpaid tax under TCAL Article 32. Any deficiency or false under-declaration can be treated as tax evasion under TCAL Article 63, resulting in recovery of the unpaid tax plus a monetary penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid CIT. Failure to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation shifts the burden of proof to the taxpayer and permits the tax authority to apply deemed adjustments, penalty interest, and the same 50%-500% evasion penalty. Criminal liability arises under Criminal Law Article 201 if fraudulent declarations conceal or understate tax with the evaded tax amount exceeding a relatively large threshold, carrying imprisonment up to 7 years for especially large amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding on gross dividends distributed by the WFOE to non-resident enterprise shareholders under PRC EIT Law Articles 3(3) and 37. Dividends paid to non-resident individuals may be subject to individual income tax at 20% unless a specific bilateral arrangement or temporary exemption applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a bilateral Double Tax Treaty (DTA) reduced rate, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction, bearing the competent authority seal and covering the relevant year; (2) file a withholding return with the PRC tax authority before the dividend is paid; (3) submit the treaty benefit self-declaration and beneficial ownership statement, demonstrating that the recipient is not a conduit; (4) prove direct shareholding and, for the most common 5% treaty rate, direct ownership of at least 25% of the WFOE's capital for the qualifying period; (5) demonstrate substantive economic activities, decision-making, employees, premises, and risk control in the treaty jurisdiction; and (6) upon approval, apply the reduced rate or pay the statutory 10% and apply for a tax treaty refund through the annual settlement procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on cross-border royalties and interest payable to non-resident enterprises is 10% on gross amounts under EIT Law Articles 3(3) and 37, with additional VAT (generally 6%) and surcharges for royalties/services treated as performed in China. Under most Chinese DTAs, the treaty rate for royalties and interest is 10%; some treaties provide 5% or exemption for interest paid to governmental institutions or banks, and certain copyright royalties may also be reduced. The same TRC, beneficial ownership, and withholding-before-remittance procedure must be followed to apply the treaty rate. For intercompany loans, thin-capitalisation rules limit deductible interest to the general 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio unless the taxpayer proves arm's length financing.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File contemporaneous documentation is mandatory when related-party transactions in the prior fiscal year exceed: RMB 200 million for tangible-asset transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible-asset transfers; RMB 100 million for financial-asset transfers; or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions. Master File preparation is required when the MNE group's consolidated revenue in the prior year exceeds RMB 2 billion, and Country-by-Country Reporting is required when the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply an OECD-style Bahamas/Dubai Economic Substance Regulation regime, but the PRC tax law requires economic substance through the general anti-avoidance rules (EIT Law Articles 47-48), the beneficial ownership doctrine under SAT Public Notice No. 9 of 2018, and the substance-over-form principle. For a VC GP, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) include investment sourcing, due diligence, valuation, negotiation, capital calls, portfolio management, risk monitoring, and carried-interest decision-making. If those activities are actually performed by personnel in the WFOE while profits are booked or shifted offshore, the SAT may attribute income to a permanent establishment, recharacterize the arrangement, impose transfer pricing adjustments, and deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE GP deliberately inflates management fees, consulting fees, or carried-interest allocations to an affiliated offshore fund or Hong Kong/Singapore intermediary with no real activity, thereby shifting Chinese-source profits offshore and underpaying PRC CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC EIT Law Articles 41 and 48 empower the SAT to make an arm's length recharacterization, increase taxable income, and collect unpaid tax plus benchmark-rate-plus interest. Under TCAL Article 63, intentional evasion attracts a monetary penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, daily late-payment surcharges, and, if the amount is sufficiently large, criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, CFOs, and legal representatives who sign false returns or direct the booking of sham fees risk being named as directly responsible persons under Criminal Law Article 201 and Article 211, with imprisonment up to 3 years for relatively large evasion and up to 7 years for especially large evasion, plus fines. Civilly, if corporate assets are stripped to avoid tax, courts may pierce the corporate veil under Company Law Article 23, causing directors/shareholders to return extracted assets and make good unpaid taxes. The tax authority may also blacklist the legal representative and impose travel restrictions/exit bans under the outstanding-tax enforcement measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-Company / Treaty Abuse / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a non-resident intermediary without premises, personnel, decision-making power, or risk control to hold the WFOE shares and receive dividends, royalties, or interest while claiming a DTA reduced rate, or maintaining the WFOE itself as a hollow entity with no real VC GP operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The claim for treaty relief is rejected under SAT Public Notice No. 9 of 2018 for failure to satisfy the beneficial ownership test. EIT Law Articles 47-48 allow the SAT to apply GAAR to disregard the intermediary, recharacterize the income, impose the statutory 10% WHT, add interest, and apply TCAL Article 63 penalties of 50% to 500% of underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly create a sham conduit may lose the protection of limited liability: under Company Law Article 23, if abuse of the company's legal personality is used to evade tax, the controlling shareholder and those acting in concert are jointly and severally liable for company debts and tax arrears. The legal representative can be placed on the tax blacklist, banned from travel, and debarred from new senior management roles; criminal liability can arise if the arrangement is part of fraudulent tax evasion, carrying up to 7 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Failure / Unreported Outbound Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE remits dividends, interests, royalties, or carried-interest distributions to non-resident investors without filing the PRC withholding return and without paying the statutory 10% WHT or the applicable treaty rate, or without obtaining a TRC and beneficial ownership evidence before the date of payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under TCAL Article 69, the withholding agent that fails to withhold is ordered to remit the unpaid tax and is fined 50% to 300% of the failed withholding; the foreign payee may also be pursued for the tax. If the withholding agent fails to pay after demand, daily late-payment surcharges of 0.05% accrue under TCAL Article 32. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 can apply where the failure is intentional and large.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and financial officers who order or authorize dividend remittances without WHT face civil liability for the unpaid collection if they are found to have abused the corporate form or acted outside corporate interests; the company may be required to withhold from subsequent distributions. The legal representative and CFO may be blacklisted, denied exit, and have personal assets traced where funds are commingled or transferred for personal benefit. In egregious cases, personal criminal penalties of imprisonment for tax evasion of up to 3-7 years and monetary fines are imposed under Criminal Law Articles 201 and 211.
